content.text:
**Finding: Compliant** (no redline proposed)

The EXCLUSIVITY rule is satisfied at the **preferred** position — the Agreement contains no exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation binding Clear Capital.

Key points supporting this conclusion:

| Paragraph | Language | Assessment |
|---|---|---|
| p0004 (§1(a)) | Retains Contractor "on a task by task basis" via separate SOWs | Non-exclusive; no minimum volume or requirements commitment |
| p0011 (§2) | Open term, terminable under ¶6 | No exclusive-dealing period |
| p0020 (§4) | Contractor IP is its "sole and exclusive property" | IP ownership allocation, not exclusive dealing |
| p0021 (§4(c)) | "royalty-free, non-exclusive perpetual license" to Company | Grant **in our favor**, and expressly non-exclusive |
| p0051 (§17) | "complete and exclusive agreement" | Entire-agreement boilerplate |
| p0047 (§13) | Mutual 1-year non-solicit of employees | Restricts hiring, not procurement; reciprocal; separate rule |

The planner's `likelyAbsent: true` hint proved correct. I checked all three keyword-driven directions — exclusive-dealing phrasings ("sole," "requirements," "shall not procure," "third party"), non-compete/restrictive-covenant language, and the purpose-of-engagement clause itself — and none produced a covenant limiting our freedom to buy elsewhere.

Two directional judgments worth flagging, since both could have been mis-flagged: the non-exclusive license in p0021 runs **to** Clear Capital and benefits us, and §13's non-solicit is mutual and concerns personnel rather than purchasing. Neither is a deviation under this rule, and §13 should be left to whichever rule governs non-solicitation so the same term isn't flagged twice.
